{{Top|Enemy|Corpus|Corpus|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|The Amprex rifle fires a continuous beam of high voltage electricity that arcs among nearby enemies. This weapon excels at crowd control.}} The '''Amprex''' is a {{Faction|Corpus}} beam rifle that fires a continuous stream of {{D|Electricity}} arcs that can chain between units, making it a devastating crowd control weapon. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals {{D|Electricity}} damage. *{{M|Heavy Caliber}}'s [[accuracy]] penalty is minimal on this weapon. *Beam can chain up to '''3''' nearby enemies within '''10''' meters of each other, with each chain doing '''50%''' of the previous chain's damage. **Each enemy hit by the main beam from [[Punch Through]] can generate a new set of 3 chains. **Enemy corpses will still allow the beam to connect to nearby enemies. {{Advantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Held| *Second highest [[critical chance]] of all continuous and automatic primaries, behind {{Weapon|Synapse}}. *Consumes 0.5 ammo per tick of damage. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Rifle|trigger=Held| *Damage ramps up from 30% to 100% over 0.6 seconds when firing. After firing stops for 0.8 seconds, the damage decays back to 30% over 2 seconds. *Main beam has a limited range of 18 meters. **{{M|Sinister Reach}} can be equipped to extend the maximum range. *Chain beam has a limited range of 10 meters. **Chain beam range cannot be increased with {{M|Sinister Reach}}. }} ==Acquisition== The Amprex's blueprint can be [[research]]ed from the [[Research/Energy Lab|Energy Lab]] in the [[dojo]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}. ==Notes== *When fired at an enemy, the beam will chain to the closest enemy within '''10''' meters of the initial target. From there it will chain again, up to a maximum of 3 chains in total. A chain will do {{MathText|0.5{{exp|n}}}} times the main beam's damage, where '''n''' is the chain number. Any enemy caught in the width of the beam will also be damaged. **The damages are : '''100%''' for the main target, '''50%''' for the first in the chain, '''25%''' for the 2nd, and '''12.5%''' for the 3rd. **Headshotting the original target does not affect the chain damage. **The beam '''will not''' chain to a [[Nullifier Crewman|Nullifier]] through its shield should it connect with a target outside or partially enclosed by it. **The beam can also continue to chain to enemies even if targeting a dead enemy or an enemy who is dead but in a dying animation. **Additional electrical arcs are also emitted, striking randomly around the player. However, these stray arcs are purely visual in effect. *Compared to the {{Weapon|Synapse}}, the Amprex deals more damage and it continuously arcs to other enemies, making it more effective against crowds. Use the Synapse for single targets and the Amprex for crowd control. **The fire rate of Amprex is the same as Synapse, and it deals slightly more damage, however it has a 2.6s reload speed, nearly double the 1.5s reload speed of the Synapse. ==Tips== *This weapon's high [[critical chance]] and damage make it ideal for critical focused builds using {{M|Point Strike}} and {{M|Vital Sense}}. *The Amprex's high fire rate and its low base damage make it highly ammo inefficient, consuming ammo at an alarming rate. It is recommended to use {{M|Rifle Ammo Mutation}}, Carrier's {{M|Ammo Case}}, or {{M|Rifle Scavenger}} to ensure a steady supply of ammo. Alternatively, bring [[Squad Ammo Restore]]s to help replenish lost ammo. *{{M|Critical Delay}} can be used to reduce ammo consumption, increase time between reloads, and increase damage per hit, but at a cost to the weapon's DPS. *Although it is preferred to mod the weapon to other damage types, base {{D|Electricity}} damage paired with its high [[status chance]] makes for a good stunning weapon among groups, and the added damage through electrical procs that chain to other enemies. [[Infested]] have no weakness or resistance to electrical damage, making the base electrical damage work well for that faction. Forma is often required to change the damage type to match the amount of damage done by pure electrical damage, however. *Using with {{WF|Mirage}} gives you two more beams that also chain to other targets, providing much more crowd control. *Decreasing the accuracy of the Amprex with a mod like [[Heavy Caliber]] will not only increase the Amprex's damage but works well for large groups of enemies as it increases the spread of the weapons Fire. *[[Punch Through]] will cause the main beam to chain independently from each additional target hit, potentially doubling or tripling the total damage output when fired into a crowd. The chain from the target hit after the Punch Through can deal damage to the first target, and vice versa. ==Trivia== *After the clan obtains the Energy Lab, it will take exactly 12 days to research this weapon. *The Amprex's name is a portmanteau of the words [[wikipedia:Ampere|Ampere]] (the base unit of the International System of Units used to quantify electric current) and the word ''Rex'', which is the Latin word for king. **The word ampere itself is named after a French mathematician and physicist, André-Marie Ampère, who's also considered to be one of the fathers of classical electromagnetism, most commonly known for [[wikipedia:Ampère's_circuital_law|Ampère's Circuital Law]]. **Like the {{Weapon|Flux Rifle}} and {{Weapon|Detron}}, Amprex does not conform to the common [[Corpus]] weapon name scheme; two syllables ending in 'a'. *The weapon shares its similarities on its battery components with {{Weapon|Tetra}}. *This is the third Primary weapon that deals purely {{D|Electricity}} damage, after {{Weapon|Lanka}} and {{Weapon|Synapse}} (since {{ver|22.13.3}} Synapse deals {{D|Corrosive}} instead). *This is the second clan weapon that does not need a Forma in its construction. *Hatches on the side of the Amprex slowly open up during firing, spreading vanes underneath. This animation is a visual indicator of the weapon's magazine capacity, with the vanes spreading out more the closer the magazine is to empty. The hatch closes upon reloading. *This is the first weapon in [[Research/Energy Lab|Energy Lab]] whose duplication costs 50,000 credits. *After {{ver|15.13}}, the chained beams were changed to be affected by {{M|Sinister Reach}} as well. As of {{ver|22.14}}, this is no longer the case. ==Media== AmprexCodex.png|Amprex in Codex AmprexColors.jpg|Demonstration of Amprex color customization 2014-04-23_00014.jpg|Frost standing at the end of the Amprex's beam length. Took approximately 4.5 forward rolls to reach him from this distance. Screenshot_483.png|Amprex in Arsenal Screenshot_484.png|Amprex side profile {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|uuSoGrvlpbM|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|OAb2TU3c-as|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|bWoIOR8gnaA|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|5-m1paBdG68|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 60 Ammo per Pick Up: *Amprex {{ver|22.14}} *Fixed Beam weapons not being able to damage enemies (alive but in a ragdolled state) when being affected by certain ‘crowd control’ Abilities. *Damage now ramps up over 0.6 seconds and after moving off target there is a delay of 0.8 seconds before it starts to decay over 2 seconds. *All Beam weapons now start their Damage ramp up at 20% (instead of 10%). *The Multishot chance should now apply more consistently with Beam weapons. *Weapon Range Mods (like Sinister Reach) no longer affect the distance of chains for chainable Beam weapons (like the Amprex). Main Beam distance is still affected by them. *Fixed Beam weapons continuously firing when quick Meleeing. *Chain Range increased from 7.5m to 10m. *Damage reduced from 24 to 22. {{ver|22.13.4}} *Increased the Beam weapon Damage ramp up time from 0.8 to 1 second. *Fixed Beam weapon Damage ramp up not happening per target. {{ver|22.13.3}} *Perfect accuracy and high fire rate is balanced by limited range and damage ramping up from 10% to 100% over 0.8 seconds when firing and decays back to 10% over 1 second after stopping. *Mastery Rank increased from 5 to 10. *Damage increased from 7.5 to 24 . *Fire Rate decreased from 20 to 12 . *Status chance changed from 20% per sec to 22% per tick of damage. *Critical chance decreased from 50% to 32%. *Critical Damage increased from 2.0x to 2.2x. *Max ammo capacity increased from 540 to 700. *0.5 Ammo consumption per tick of damage. *Aimed Zoom reduced from 2.23x to 1.4x. {{ver|19.5}} *Magazine size in Conclave reduced from 100 to 40. {{ver|The Index Preview}} *The Amprex can now be used in Conclave. {{ver|18.8.2}} *Decreased the rumble amount on controllers when continuously firing the Amprex. {{ver|17.4}} *Fixed some lingering visual FX from Amprex when used with Mirage’s Hall of Mirrors {{ver|16.5.3}} *PBR material has been added to the Amprex! {{ver|16.4.1}} *Fixed Amprex not chaining to nearby enemies. {{ver|15.13}} *Sinister Reach will now extend the Amprex’s chain lightning effect. {{ver|14.0.11}} *Damage multipliers for the Amprex normalized. {{ver|13.3}} *Fixed an issue with the reload animation for the Amprex not properly coinciding with when the magazine was refilled. {{ver|13.1.2}} *Improved the performance of the Amprex on low end machines. *Fixed the visuals on the battery component of the Amprex rifle. {{ver|13.1}} *Introduced. }} ==See also== *{{Weapon|Synapse}}, the [[Infested]] equivalent of this weapon. *{{Weapon|Atomos}}, a Grineer particle cannon with a functionally equivalent chaining beam. *{{Weapon|Kuva Nukor}}, a Kuva Lich sidearm with a functionally equivalent chaining beam. *{{Weapon|Tenet Cycron}}, a Tenet weapon with a similar chaining beam. *{{Weapon|Larkspur}}, an [[Archgun]] with a functionally equivalent chaining beam. {{ResearchNav}} {{WeaponNav}} [[de:Amprex]] [[es:Amprex]] [[fr:Amprex]] [[pt:Amprex]] [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Primary Weapons]] [[Category:Assault Rifle]] [[Category:Research]] [[Category:Corpus]] [[Category:Electricity Damage Weapons]] [[Category:Update 13]] [[Category:Continuous Weapons]] [[uk:Ампрекс]] [[Category:Chaining Weapons]] [[Category:Chaining Projectiles]]

{{Top|Enemy|Corpus|Corpus|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|Capable of firing multiple rockets at once, the Angstrum is a handheld instrument of destruction.}} The '''Angstrum''' is a heavy sidearm of {{Faction|Corpus}} design that fires powerful micro-rockets. Its charge-based trigger allows for firing precise single shots, or emptying the entire magazine as a spread barrage for engaging single heavy targets or large groups. This weapon can be sold for {{cc|5,000}} ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals {{D|Blast}} damage. *Rocket explode in a '''3.6''' meter radius on impact with a surface or enemy. **Initial hit and explosion apply status separately. **Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls. **Can benefit from {{M|Fulmination}} ({{M|Primed Fulmination|Primed}}). *Can be charged to unload more of the weapon's magazine and fire extra projectiles. **Can be fired with a partial charge to fire only part of its magazine. **Fully charged shot consumes the entire magazine, even when magazine mods are used. **Charged barrage spreads rockets out, reducing the effective range considerably. **[[Multishot]] will cause partially-charged shots to spread out further, eliminating its long range potential. *Innate {{Pol|Vazarin}} polarity. {{Advantages| *Tied with {{Weapon|Prisma Angstrum}} for highest base damage of all secondaries. *High [[accuracy]]. }} {{Disadvantages| *Projectiles have travel time, slow speed, and are small, making long range shots difficult. *Very high recoil. *The weapon fires as soon as it has reached a full charge, which can lead to premature firing. *Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. *Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions. *Explosion has linear [[Damage Falloff]] from 100% to 60% from central impact. *Extremely poor ammo economy. **Extremely low magazine size of 3 rounds; requires frequent reloading. **Very low ammo capacity of 18 rounds. **Only restores 3 units of ammunition per ammo pickup. *Rockets have a short delay after firing before being able to fire again. *Enemies can destroy the rockets with gunfire or area of effect explosions. }} {{WeaponComparison|Prisma Angstrum}} ==Acquisition== The Angstrum's blueprint can be purchased from the [[Market]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} ==Notes== *Rockets launched by the Angstrum have an initial speed of '''0.5''' m/s, then accelerate at '''15''' m/s2 until they reach their maximum speed of '''150''' m/s. **When firing more than one rocket, they will curve outwards in a flower shape. **[[Projectile Speed]] does not affect the spread of the rockets or make them more accurate, but it does change their trajectory on the way to their destination. ***High [[Projectile Speed]] makes them fly in a straight line towards their destination, spreading out immediately like a shotgun. ***Low [[Projectile Speed]] makes them stick together in a line for a few meters before blossoming outwards in a curved trajectory. **Although single rockets are very accurate, firing multiple rockets is drastically affected by [[Accuracy]] penalties such as from [[Magnum Force]]. *Tapping the trigger will auto charge and fire a single rocket; holding the trigger will charge a shot that adds an additional rocket for every '''0.5''' seconds the trigger is held. Added shots are limited by the current magazine capacity. **Added rockets will consume an equivalent amount of magazine. **Charged shots cannot be held; the Angstrum will fire as soon as it is fully charged. **Use the reload button or changing weapons will cancel charged shots. **Unlike a shotgun which shoots a completely random spread, the Angstrum is shown to form a geometrical structure (depending on the rocket quantity) of:{{Column|2| ***One - A single accurate shot. ***Two - Two separate horizontal shots. ***Three - A triangle. ***Four - Diagonal square. ***Five - Pentagon. ***Six - Triangle with an offset center triangle. ***Seven - Diagonal square with a center triangle. ***Eight - Pentagon with an offset center triangle. ***Nine - Hexagon with a center triangle. ***Ten - Heptagon with a center triangle. ***Eleven - Octagon with a center triangle ***Twelve - Outer diagonal square, middle pentagon, center triangle ***Thirteen - Outer pentagon, middle pentagon, center triangle ***Fourteen - Outer hexagon, middle pentagon, center triangle ***Fifteen - Outer heptagon, middle pentagon, center triangle ***Sixteen - Outer octagon, middle pentagon, center triangle ***Seventeen - Outer enneagon, middle pentagon, center triangle ***Eighteen - Outer decagon, middle pentagon, center triangle ***Nineteen - Outer hendecagon, middle pentagon, center triangle ***Twenty - Outer dodecagon, middle pentagon, center triangle }} *Angstrum's shots bounce off [[Nullifier Crewman|Nullifiers']] barriers rather than exploding, and will detonate upon hitting another solid object. Beware as this includes the player who fired it. ==Incarnon Genesis== {{Transclude|Angstrum Incarnon Genesis#Acquisition}} {{Transclude|Angstrum Incarnon Genesis#Incarnon Genesis}} ==Tips== *Use {{M|Magnum Force}} if you wish to cover a greater area, as the damage bonus granted by this mod can help counteract any loss of damage due to the accuracy penalty. Bear in mind this is at the expense of the Angstrum's charged shots at long range. *{{M|Fulmination}} can also be used to fill a target area more completely as the increased blast radius provided by it will counteract the empty spaces in between spread out charged shots. *To more accurately hit a group of targets, Bullet Jump straight up and aim glide at the targeted area and then fully charging up your shot so all of the individual rockets will connect and explode on contact with the ground. This way, the explosion will do much more damage spread out over a consistent area rather than just shooting on the floor. *If charged and/or a [[Multishot]] mod is equipped ({{M|Barrel Diffusion}}, {{M|Lethal Torrent}}), the rockets will fire in a precise shape based on how many rockets are fired, making it easier to aim. *Increasing the magazine size will result in a higher projectile count when firing a totally charged shot. Bear in mind that increasing the magazine size will also increase the time it takes to charge the shot. **Using {{M|Slip Magazine}}, {{M|Ice Storm}}, and {{M|Tainted Clip}} will increase the Angstrum's magazine to 7 (rounded from 6.9). ***With {{M|Primed Slip Magazine}}, it can reach 8 rockets **Combining the magazine build with {{M|Barrel Diffusion}} and/or Lethal Torrent will yield the chance of a totally charged shot firing 21 projectiles. ***With the above primed mod, it can reach 24. **Using the previous combination with {{WF|Mirage}}'s {{A|Hall of Mirrors}} can yield a total of 63 projectiles in one salvo. This is obviously not recommended for low configs. ***Can reach 72 if chances play out. *{{M|Gunslinger}} and/or Lethal Torrent speeds up the charge time, allowing for faster firing rates. This is especially important if one is maximizing magazine capacity, as the charge time for a large magazine can be long. *{{WF|Mag}}'s {{A|Magnetize}} synergizes well with this weapon, as it allows all the rockets fired to be redirected unto a single target, dealing massive amounts of damage. This is most useful against heavy units like [[Napalm]]s, and against bosses that have no weak spots like [[Ambulas]]. *It is highly recommended to equip a {{M|Pistol Ammo Mutation}} mod to remove practically all ammunition problems. *{{M|Lethal Momentum}} can increase rocket velocity by up to 40%, significantly reducing the amount of lead time required for distant targets. *The innate {{Pol|Vazarin}} polarity can somewhat limit elemental modding potential, thus making it a less desirable polarity for elemental modding. If you wish to focus more on elemental damage, then it is recommended to either ignore the polarity or use [[Forma]] to turn it into a more suitable polarity. **Putting {{M|Deep Freeze}} and making use of the secondary elemental damages that use Cold damage can make use of this polarity. ==Trivia== *The Angstrum's name is derived from [[wikipedia:Angstrom|Angstrom]], which is a unit of measurement that is 0.1 nanometers in length. *This weapon appears to be of [[Corpus]] design, making it their second explosive weapon following the {{Weapon|Penta}}. *When charging, the rockets in the chamber lower into the gun itself. *The Angstrum's concept of a conventional-appearing weapon (pistol in this case) firing rockets is similar to that of the [[wikipedia:Gyrojet|Gyrojet]] from the 1960s. *Its boxy design is similar to the [[wikipedia:Uzi|IMI Uzi MP-2]] machine pistol, including the way the weapon can be held. *The market icon for additional weapon slots depicts the silhouette of an Angstrum alongside a [[Scindo]] ==Media== AngstrumCodex.png|Angstrum in Codex.   {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|I06aO5tOcMI|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|Vo_oDd_srHc|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|dXQIVMRsfMg|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|Ei66Vt5G96s|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|OAb2TU3c-as|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Secondary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 3 Ammo per Pick Up: *Angstrum ;Headshot Damage Changes During playtesting, the ammo changes alone weren’t enough to significantly change things for AoE weapons. So instead of tightening these values to be overly restrictive, we chose to address other factors that make these weapons so strong, such as headshot damage. Our approach here is two-fold, to reduce the impact of headshots for AOE weapons, but to also make precision headshots pack a larger punch overall. *Radial damage no longer gains extra headshot damage or triggers headshot conditions. **This is primarily targeted at the Ignis Wraith - as a “flamethrower” weapon, it’s hard to imagine a blanket of elements being precise enough to target weak points specifically. Explosive projectiles themselves can still land headshots, so there is still a reason to aim with most weapons for maximum damage. {{ver|27.2.2}}
Reduced the following AoE weapons Radial Damage Falloff from central impact that were all previously 90%: *Angstrum: 40% {{ver|27.2}} ;Self Damage Changes: We are getting rid of Self Damage and replacing it with something else: instead of Self Damage, it’s now ‘Stagger’. This change completely removes the chance of killing yourself, and instead now creates scenarios where you will interrupt yourself - or ‘Stagger’ - to varying degrees if you aren’t careful. The degrees of Self-Interrupt start with a small stumble all the way to full knockdown depending on how close you are to the center of explosion. Any Mods referring to Self Damage will be converted to acknowledge Stagger. With this Self-Interrupt system, we have added dozens of new recovery animations that harness a ninja-like recovery experience. By pressing ‘Jump’ at the correct time, you can execute a ninja-skill-based knockdown recovery to ALL in-game knockdowns. This ninja recovery window is indicated by a glowing FX on your Warframe. In the original Dev Workshop, we said:
''As a result of this overall systemic change, Weapons with Stagger will be getting approximately a 20% buff in Damage, with any weapons with AOE receiving a 50% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact.'' This is no longer accurate after continued testing. What we are doing now is: No damage buffs have been added, but any weapons with AOE are receiving ~20% increase in Radius. Additionally, AOE weapons are receiving a 90% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact. This means on the very outer section of the explosion Radius 10% of the Damage will be dealt. Tactics will be deadly - aim true, Tenno. ''Why: Several players brought up the history of the Tonkor and we want to make sure we ship this change in a place that’s conservative in its starting point from a balance perspective. The complete removal of Self Damage does change the pace of destruction with some of the game’s most powerful weapons, so we want to make sure we can iterate upwardly instead of releasing a bonanza of explosions with no other choices.'' ;Greater than 100% Status having meaning: Shotguns have a unique Role here based on a very patch-work history with how they interact with Status Chance. A Shotgun that shoots 99% Status Chance would give you 35% (roughly) status per pellet. 100% Status Gives you 100% Status per pellet. This huge jump in performance happens with just a 1% gain - why? Well, to answer that we have to look at our choice to make what the UI conveys reality. It would feel broken to shoot a Shotgun with 100% Status and not see a perfect spread of Effects. In reality, to make Status consistent we have to treat Shotguns as a special case. Shotguns as a special case means we have buffed the Status Chance of all Shotguns by x3 or greater. The UI now behaves to show the reality that you are determining Status Chance per pellet. {{ver|23.0.3}} *Fixed Angstrum not having any shooting sounds. {{ver|22.12}} *Direct Impact damage increased from 175 to 200. *Status chance increased from 10 to 22%. *Critical chance increased from 5% to 16%. *Ammo capacity decreased from 30 to 18. {{ver|22}} *Improved the mesh quality of the Angstrum to avoid blocky textures. *Fixed Clients not seeing the Host's Angstrum ammo magazine cycle correctly. {{ver|21.6}} *Improved the Angstrum's explosion FX. {{ver|21}} *Fixed the Angstrum generating infinite spread for its first shot. *Fixed Angstrum's charge animation not loading bullets into the weapon chamber. {{ver|20}} *Fixed a visual bug for Clients where the charged shots of the Angstrum would appear to fire twice. {{ver|TSG}} *Angstrum damage and projectile speed increased in Conclave. {{ver|Lunaro}} *Fixed hearing fully charged sounds when firing the Angstrums last shot. {{ver|18.6.2}} *Fixed the Angstrum not playing the proper audio FX when charging up. {{ver|18.6}} *Fixed Angstrum displaying incorrect noise level in the Arsenal. {{ver|18.5}} *Angstrum Conclave skin now available. *Increased the damage of the Angstrum in Conclave. {{ver|18.4.10}} *Removed the headshot multiplier from the Angstrum in Conclave. *Increased the Angstrum's initial projectile speed in Conclave. *Reduced the Angstrum's ammo pool in Conclave. *The Angstrum's explosive damage no longer ignores cover in Conclave. {{ver|17.9}} *Angstrum Day of the Dead Skin is now available. {{ver|17.5}} *Angstrum damage increased in PvP. *The Angstrum has received the PBR treatment! {{ver|16.11}} *Fixed the Angstrum always showing as having 0 magazine capacity. {{ver|16.4}} *The Angstrum has been balanced for use in PvP. {{ver|14.2}} **Base ammo increased to 30 (from proposed 21) considering the volume of projectiles launched. {{ver|14.0.5}} *Performance Improvements for Mirage + Hall of Mirrors and Angstrum. {{ver|13.3.1}} *Fixed multishot mods not allowing for random chance of extra rocket when applied to Angstrum. {{ver|13.3}} *Introduced. }} {{ver/Lu|24.1.5}} ==See also== *[[Comba]] and [[Scrambus]], corpus enemies who often wield modified versions of the weapon. {{WeaponNav}} [[de:Angstrum]] [[es:Angstrum]] [[fr:Angstrum]] [[Category:Secondary Weapons]] [[Category:Corpus]] [[Category:Update 13]] [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Launcher]] [[Category:Launcher (Secondary)]] [[Category:Single Sidearm]] [[uk:Анґструм]] [[Category:Blast Damage Weapons]]

{{ModBox}}
'''Anemic Agility''' is a [[Corrupted Mods|Corrupted Mod]] that increases a pistol's [[fire rate]] by 15% per rank but decreases its [[damage]] by 2.5% per rank, for a maximum of 90% fire rate and -15% damage at rank 5.

==Stats==

==Notes==
*Dodge Speed increases the speed the player moves at when rolling.
*Has a hidden Acrobatic Speed bonus, which increases the rate at which you roll, resulting in a shorter roll duration.
**Together, the Dodge Speed and Acrobatic Speed bonuses result in a roll that goes approximately the same distance as a normal roll while taking less time.
**The quicker roll animation can benefit {{M|Rolling Guard}}, maximizing the invulnerability period by reducing the time wasted while rolling.
*The both bonuses are applied universally so long as Amalgam Barrel Diffusion is installed on the currently carried Secondary weapon; you do not need to be aiming, or even have your secondary wielded, to make use of the bonuses.
*Amalgam Barrel Diffusion is essentially the {{M|Barrel Diffusion}} mod with altered stats. It is considered the same mod as its normal counterpart, and thus both mods cannot be equipped together.
*Cannot be equipped on [[Sentinel]] weapons.
*Synergizes well with {{WF|Limbo}}, allowing him to slide between the material plane and [[Rift Plane]] more quickly.
*The mod in reality grants 109.50% multishot, however the text and tooltip round up to 110%.

{{Codex|Bring negotiations to an instant conclusion with this Corpus assault rifle. Switch effortlessly between charged explosive sniper shots and rapid fire electrical assault mode}}

The '''Ambassador''' is a [[Corpus]] assault rifle whose [[Alternate Fire]] allows switching between fully-automatic rounds or a long-ranged explosive shot.

==Characteristics==
*This weapon primarily deals {{D|Electricity}} damage.
*[[Alternate Fire]] mode-switching reloads the weapon and changes the weapon's firing mode to a charged shot.
*Charge mode:
**Pinpoint accuracy.
***{{M|Heavy Caliber}}'s accuracy penalty is minimal.
**Shots explode in a '''6''' meter radius on impact with a surface or enemy.
***Initial hit and explosion apply status separately.
***Explosion does not need direct line of sight to deal damage and will penetrate walls.
***Can benefit from {{M|Firestorm}} ({{M|Primed Firestorm|Primed}}) and {{M|Cautious Shot}}.
**Charge is automatic and does not need to be held down.
***However, holding down the trigger will not fire the shot at full charge thus allowing for aim adjustments. 
***Rolling while holding the full charge will cancel it and not consume any ammo.
**Consumes 16 ammo per shot, effectively resulting in a 6-round magazine.

{{Advantages|
}}

{{Disadvantages|
*Charge mode:
**Explosion inflicts [[Stagger|self-stagger]].
**Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of 1x and cannot trigger headshot conditions.
**Explosion has linear [[Damage Falloff]] from 100% to 50% from central impact.
*[[Alternate Fire]] mode-switching is '''not''' instantaneous and has an animation equal to the reload speed.
}}

{{Acquisition|This weapon's main blueprint can be acquired from Rotation C of [[Empyrean]] [[Survival]] missions in [[Venus Proxima]], [[Neptune Proxima]], [[Pluto Proxima]], and [[Veil Proxima]]. The component blueprints are dropped by [[Aurax Atloc Raknoid]]s and [[Narmer Raknoid]]s. All parts can be [[Trading|traded]] between players.}}
{{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}}

==Notes==
*[[Alternate Fire]] mode switching is affected by [[reload speed]] mods.
**While this makes it so the weapon will always fire six shots when on charge mode, the weapon will not fire if the magazine has less than 48 rounds, and will reload automatically instead.
***{{M|Tainted Mag}} gives the weapon enough rounds to fire more shots in charge mode, at the cost of decreased reload and switch speed.
***{{M|Primed Magazine Warp}} also gives the weapon enough rounds to fire more shots in charge mode, without reducing reload speed. If kept at rank 9, it provides exactly 48 rounds and will thus begin automatically reloading after nine shots.

==Trivia==
*The [[Machinist]]'s weapon is identical in appearance to the Ambassador, however theirs functions as a flamethrower rather than a laser assault rifle.
*In automatic fire mode, the weapon will become quieter with less reverb once the magazine goes below 48 ammo, as well as the standard sound cue that the magazine is running low. 
*The Ambassador does not replace its magazine on reload. Reloading the gun appears to involve the magazine being taken out, banged twice against the ejection port, and then simply replaced in the magazine slot.

{{ver|32}}
;Headshot Damage Changes
During playtesting, the ammo changes alone weren’t enough to significantly change things for AoE weapons. So instead of tightening these values to be overly restrictive, we chose to address other factors that make these weapons so strong, such as headshot damage. 

Our approach here is two-fold, to reduce the impact of headshots for AOE weapons, but to also make precision headshots pack a larger punch overall.

*Radial damage no longer gains extra headshot damage or triggers headshot conditions.
**This is primarily targeted at the Ignis Wraith - as a “flamethrower” weapon, it’s hard to imagine a blanket of elements being precise enough to target weak points specifically. Explosive projectiles themselves can still land headshots, so there is still a reason to aim with most weapons for maximum damage.
